AEM Holdings Has Delivered 443%+ Returns YTD: What’s Next?
article:
AEM Holdings
(SGX: AWX) delivered a total return of over 443% year to date as of last Friday (18 September 2026), according to Fiscal.ai.
AEM makes test handlers and systems for the semiconductor industry.
A return of 443% in under nine months is eye-catching.
The company’s first-half results provide reasons why the stock is gaining.
What drove AEM’s first-half performance?
Revenue rose 29.9% year on year to S$247.2 million for the first half of 2026 (1H 2026).
Net profit hit S$31 million, a 10-fold increase from S$3.1 million a year ago.
The margin expansion is worth highlighting.
Gross margin rose from 25.4% to 33.1% on a better segment mix, leading to net margin reaching 12.5%, up from 1.6% in 1H 2025.
Test Cell Solutions drove the results.
Revenue from this segment grew 52.5% year on year to S$180.9 million, around 73% of group revenue.
A single fabless AI and high-performance computing (HPC) customer became AEM’s top revenue contributor for the half.
This is a meaningful shift.
The message?
AEM’s revenue base is broadening beyond its traditional PC/Foundry customer.
This is an important development, as the business is becoming less concentrated and
more diversified
.
The dividend reward
AEM last declared an
interim dividend
in 1H 2022.
Four years on, it paid S$0.024 per share for 1H 2026.
Management could have stuck with a once-a-year final dividend.
It chose to bring back the interim.
That tells you it expects to keep paying.
Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to S$630 million to S$680 million, up from S$550 million to S$600 million.
AEM attributed the increase to its fabless AI/HPC ramp and its PC/Foundry customer’s adoption of the Asynchronous Modular Parallel Smart (AMPS) platform.
For the first time, AEM also guided towards earnings per share of between S$0.245 and S$0.275.
Where does AEM’s growth go from here?
AEM has built its strategy around five business pillars.
Source: AEM’s 1H 2026 earnings presentation
Two are already contributing to revenue and margins.
Three are still in development.
Pillar 01 centres on its PC/Foundry customer.
AEM does not name this customer, but it is widely presumed to be
Intel
(NASDAQ: INTC).
The semiconductor equipment maker plans to expand the installed fleet through Test 1.5 upgrades.
The harder future insertions would go to Test 2.0.
It’s worth decoding these labels.
Think of the configurables and collaterals under Test 1.5 as the razor blades.
The full systems and handlers under Test 2.0 are the razors.
AEM is building a razor-and-razor blade business.
Pillar 02 targets its PC/AI fabless customer.
Most analysts point to
Advanced Micro Devices
(NASDAQ: AMD) as the likely name.
AEM aims to sustain the high-volume ramp and gradually shift more demanding insertions onto its own solutions.
The semiconductor firm credits these two pillars for its raised 2026 guidance.
The company’s order backlog for the AMPS platform now exceeds S$400 million, and both the AI/HPC fabless and PC/Foundry customers continue to add orders.
The remaining three pillars still need to prove themselves.
Pillar 03 (Memory) requires AEM to qualify its Xact handler at its first memory integrated device manufacturer (IDM).
The ramp is pencilled in for 2027.
This would mark AEM’s entry into the memory testing market.
Pillar 04 taps on outsourced semiconductor assembly and test companies (OSATs) and runs through
ASE Technology
(NYSE: ASX).
AEM’s approach is to track the chiplet as it moves through AI/HPC OSATs.
The channel gives AEM a path to hyperscalers it could not have reached alone.
Pillar 05 (Contract Manufacturing) aims to support AEM’s semiconductor ramp and lift its own profitability.
What about the cash flow?
Income investors
, though, have their eyes on AEM’s free cash flow.
And for good reason.
AEM’s free cash flow fell to just S$2 million in 1H 2026, down from S$37.4 million a year ago.
Operating cash flow dropped to S$12.5 million from S$46.4 million a year ago.
Where did the cash go?
Inventories consumed S$37.6 million and receivables another S$31.5 million.
Management says the inventory build supports second-half growth.
AEM has S$80 million in net cash to cover its dividend obligations.
Get Smart: Priced for the future, not the past
AEM grew net profit 10-fold in 1H 2026.
But its free cash flow fell to S$2 million.
Profit without cash flow is a promise, not proof.
To be fair, the future looks promising.
Two of AEM’s five pillars are delivering, and the AMPS backlog tops S$400 million.
For investors looking for dividends, the milestone to watch is whether AEM can convert profits into cash.
With more cash, the chances of higher dividends rise.

title: Oil extends slump on Iran talks optimism, Saudi pipeline restart
article:
(Sept 23) : Oil extended losses as the US flagged progress in talks with Iran to end their war, and Saudi Arabia moved to restart a key pipeline.

West Texas Intermediate for November fell below US$90 a barrel after losing more than 10% over the previous five days, while Brent settled above US$99 on Tuesday. President Donald Trump said officials had a “very productive” meeting with Iranian envoys, even after he threatened to annihilate the Islamic Republic during a UN speech. Further meetings are planned, he added.

In the Middle East, Saudi Arabia aims to restore oil exports via its critical East-West pipeline in the coming days, enabling Riyadh to resume a bypass of the Strait of Hormuz. The conduit — which has the capacity to transport 7 million barrels a day — was damaged in attacks earlier this month.

Oil has still rallied by more than 60% this year as Middle East hostilities disrupted shipments through Hormuz, the world’s most critical energy chokepoint. The surge has boosted inflation, with product prices rallying even more than crude. Amid the fuels crunch, Trump said he had encouraged his advisers to support a ban on US diesel exports.

WTI traded 0.7% lower at US$89.89 a barrel at 6:01 a.m. in Singapore.

title: Nasdaq 100 eyes peak, oil falls on US-Iran talks
article:
(Sept 23) : A renewed rally in chipmakers drove the Nasdaq 100 toward its first record since June, with the stock market also bolstered by hopes for diplomatic efforts to end the war in Iran.

Equities bounced as President Donald Trump said US officials had a “very good” meeting with Iranian envoys in New York. A closely watched gauge of semiconductor powerhouses like Micron Technology Inc. and Nvidia Corp. climbed for a sixth straight day. The advance in tech firms offset a selloff in bank shares. Brent crude dropped to around US$99. Bonds stabilized.

Trump said the three-hour meeting — held on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meeting — was “very productive” and that another was being planned for the near future. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi attended a meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Axios reported.

The US administration has signaled a renewed effort to bring the war in the Middle East to a close, with Trump claiming in his speech that the conflict will end just after November’s US midterm elections.

“Focus will stay on geopolitics, and if there’s any confirmation of progress towards a ceasefire between the US and Iran, look for oil and yields to fall further and for stocks to rally,” said Tom Essaye at The Sevens Report.

Wall Street is also gearing up for this week’s summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, which will offer the leaders of the world’s two largest economies a chance to improve personal ties and look for common ground on contentious topics.

See also: Stocks jump on AI optimism as AMD tops US$1 trillion

Meta Platforms Inc.’s Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg is set to attend a White House state dinner for the Chinese leader, according to a person familiar with the planning. He’ll join Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm Inc. head Cristiano Amon. OpenAI President Greg Brockman will also attend, the ChatGPT maker said Monday, alongside CEO Sam Altman.

Microsoft Corp. CEO Satya Nadella will be there as well, according to a person familiar with the matter. On Friday, US officials said Amazon.com Inc. founder Jeff Bezos, Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk and Alphabet Inc. chief Sundar Pichai will be at the event. Apple Executive Chairman Tim Cook is also set to attend the dinner on Sept. 24, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday.

Traders also kept a close eye on the latest remarks from central bank officials.

See also: Oil steadies after four-day drop as traders look to Hormuz flows

Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Tom Barkin warned it could take time for inflationary shocks to wane. His Boston counterpart Susan Collins said she supported last week’s decision to raise rates, adding it would help bring inflation back to the target.

title: Apple developing new fitness tracker aimed at rivalling Whoop — Bloomberg
article:
(Sept 23): Apple Inc is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker similar to Whoop Inc’s wrist-worn device, part of an effort to rethink its smartwatch lineup and add new wearable technologies.

The company has been exploring the category for several months and is now developing prototypes, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The effort has support from top executives, but Apple hasn’t decided whether to release the product, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the work is confidential.

The project remains in a preliminary phase known internally as a technology investigation. If Apple proceeds with a release, the device likely won’t debut before 2028. A spokesperson for the Cupertino, California-based company declined to comment.

Shares of Garmin Ltd, a seller of fitness bands, fell as much as 2.5% to a session low after Bloomberg reported on the plan. Apple was up about 1% at US$342.29 as of 12.26pm in New York trading.

The prototypes feature a thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module. The absence of a screen would distinguish the device from the Apple Watch, a display-centric product that combines fitness tracking with apps, notifications and other functions.

See also: US stock rally falters near record as oil fluctuates

The market for screenless fitness bands now includes Garmin, Whoop and Google.

The potential Whoop rival has drawn particular interest from Apple executive chairman Tim Cook and services chief Eddy Cue, the people said. The latter executive took over the company’s health efforts late last year.

Though Apple remains a top seller of smartwatches — especially in the US — competitors such as Whoop and smart ring maker Oura Inc are growing quickly, with millions of users each. Their rise is prompting Apple to reconsider its approach to health and fitness tracking.

See also: Wendy’s says bankrupt franchisee lost brand rights to stores

At the same time, a leadership transition is underway at Apple’s watch and health businesses. Jeff Williams, the former chief operating officer who oversaw both areas, retired at the end of last year. Stan Ng, who led marketing for the Apple Watch and health, and Jay Blahnik, who ran Apple’s fitness strategy, have also left the company.

Cue has pushed Apple’s health team to adopt features from the newer rivals, whose products offer simpler interfaces focused squarely on fitness and health tracking. The Apple Watch serves a broader range of purposes.

Apple has already begun incorporating Whoop-style features into its latest Watch and revamped Health app. Those include more advanced heart-rate tracking and metrics that assess users’ readiness for the day. And the technology can estimate a person’s biological age based on health data.

The new app also has a cleaner, easier-to-understand interface, reflecting the influence of rival offerings.

Oura filed for an initial public offering this month, and Whoop — now valued at about US$10 billion — has told Bloomberg News that it is considering an eventual IPO.

Alphabet Inc’s Google has also entered the screenless wearables market with the recent launch of the Fitbit Air. Garmin, a pioneer of location-tracking and fitness devices, offers smart bands without displays as well.

Members of Apple’s Vision hardware team have participated in the new tracker’s early engineering work. That group developed the Vision Pro headset and is working on other wearables, including Apple’s first smart glasses and AirPods with cameras, both targeted for a 2027 release.

Apple has also been working on an artificial intelligence (AI) pendant with a camera, though that project has been postponed. The device was conceived as something users could wear as a necklace, attach to clothing or place elsewhere on the body, gathering visual data for processing by the new Siri AI assistant.

Apple is making other efforts to weave AI into its products. Earlier this month, the company introduced a watch that can record audio throughout the day and use AI to generate summaries of a wearer’s conversations and activities.

The company is also working on a major update to its smartwatch lineup for release as early as late 2027. This redesign would follow years of more incremental changes. Apple made its main watch thinner with the Series 10 two years ago, but the larger Ultra model has retained the same look since its debut four years ago.

title: US stock rally falters near record as oil fluctuates
article:
(Sept 23): A sense of caution prevailed on Wall Street after a rally that put stocks on the verge of their all-time highs, with oil prices wavering as traders looked for signs of diplomatic efforts to revive the Strait of Hormuz.

The S&P 500 was little changed. A closely watched gauge of chipmakers climbed for a sixth straight day, poised for the longest winning streak since April. A measure of big banks lost 2.2%. Brent crude hovered near US$100. Treasury yields edged up ahead of a US$69 billion sale of two-year notes. The dollar rose.

President Donald Trump said he believes the US will make a deal with Iran after the election, adding that more oil is flowing than at any point since the war started while noting prices will plummet when the conflict is over. He addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

“What happens this week may become critical for the direction of crude oil prices over the medium term,” said Thierry Wizman at Macquarie Group. “That’s because the key actors in the US-Iran war will be having meetings in New York.”

Any agreements that come out of those discussions may determine whether the conflict continues and intensifies or whether an off-ramp is found, he added.

See also: Wendy’s says bankrupt franchisee lost brand rights to stores

After his speech on Tuesday, Trump was due to meet Gulf state leaders, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, before later hosting a reception for other leaders and sitting down with Venezuela’s Delcy Rodriguez.

He’s set to return to Washington late on Tuesday, ahead of a visit by China’s Xi Jinping.

See also: DoorDash to pay US$132 mil in NYC over missing wages

Traders also kept a close eye on the latest remarks from central bank officials.

Federal Reserve Bank of Boston president Susan Collins said she supported last week’s decision to raise interest rates, which she said would help bring inflation back to the 2% target.

Her New York counterpart John Williams noted the shift to central clearing for US Treasuries and Treasury-collateralised repurchase agreements was ahead of schedule.

“Leadership has rotated decisively back towards semiconductors and hyperscalers, giving the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 enough to keep pushing higher without signs of an outright upside chase, but a more convincing rally requires broader participation,” says Michael Ball, Macro Strategist, Markets Live at Bloomberg strategists.

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The S&P 500 was little changed as of 12.02pm New York time
• The MSCI World Index was little changed
